editor_note: Entry 76 is faithful: "Anong computational state superposition ang katumbas ng isang QFT na may mga peak sa bawat odd na binary number?" keeps the direction of the question (which input state gives these QFT peaks) and uses "peak", the same word as the answer in entry 77.

In entry 107, "instantly" became "nang mabilis" (quickly) and "is not instant" became "ay hindi mabilis" (is not fast). The English contrasts the instant transfer of the quantum state with classical communication, which is not instantaneous. The Tagalog makes the state transfer merely "fast" and says the classical communication is "slow", which is a false claim, so a learner would come away with the wrong idea about where the delay comes from. Two smaller problems: in 107, "break qubits off the processor" became "hatiin" (divide or split), and in 103, "right-most" became just "kanan". Entries 80, 102 and 113 are faithful.

examples.why: 'mabilis' means fast, not instantaneous. 'Hindi mabilis' says classical communication is slow, which is false and not what the source says. The source's point is that it is not instantaneous.

That breaks the step-by-step imperative pattern of the other two cells ("Ulitin…", "Kumuha…"). A native editor would write "I-Pauli-twirl ang mga layer ng two-qubit gate".

editor_note: Entry 10 keeps the English meaning. editor_note: The caveat paragraph [59] mistranslates "this filter changes the operator being evolved" as "binabago ng filter na ito ang operator na kino-convert" ("the operator being converted"). That is the sentence explaining why diagonal-term filtering breaks the qDRIFT guarantees, and a learner could take it to mean the fermion-to-qubit conversion rather than time evolution. Several math and physics verbs also shift meaning: in [20] "absorbed into h_i" becomes "naiuukol sa $h_i$" ("pertains to"), in [57] "reduces to Z rotations" becomes "nababawas sa" ("gets diminished to"), and in [26] "evolves for duration λt/n" becomes "umuunlad" ("progresses/improves"). There are also smaller calques: "sa mga terminong excitation groups" for "in terms of" in [61] clashes with the Hamiltonian "termino", "sa ibang pagkakataon" is used for "later in the circuit" in [59], and "pito $\alpha$" should be "pitong" in [39] and [65].

examples.source: this filter changes the operator being evolved
examples.translation: binabago ng filter na ito ang operator na kino-convert
examples.suggested: binabago ng filter na ito ang operator na ini-evolve (ang operator ng time evolution)
examples.why: 'Evolved' became 'converted'. This hides the key caveat that the circuits no longer approximate evolution under the full Hamiltonian, and it suggests the fermion-to-qubit mapping instead.

examples.source: Any signed or complex prefactor is absorbed into $h_i$
examples.translation: Anumang may-sign o complex na prefactor ay naiuukol sa $h_i$
examples.suggested: Anumang may-sign o complex na prefactor ay isinasama (ina-absorb) sa $h_i$
examples.why: 'Naiuukol' means 'pertains to', so the idea that the sign or phase is folded into h_i (which keeps c_i positive) is lost.

examples.source: whose time evolution reduces to single-qubit $Z$ rotations
examples.translation: na ang time evolution ay nababawas sa single-qubit $Z$ rotations
examples.suggested: na ang time evolution ay nauuwi sa single-qubit $Z$ rotations
examples.why: 'Nababawas' means 'is diminished/subtracted', not the mathematical 'reduces to' (simplifies to).

examples.source: each of the $n$ steps evolves for the same duration $\lambda t / n$
examples.translation: bawat isa sa $n$ na hakbang ay umuunlad sa parehong tagal
examples.suggested: bawat isa sa $n$ na hakbang ay nag-e-evolve sa parehong tagal
examples.why: 'Umuunlad' means 'progresses/develops', which is the wrong sense for time evolution.

examples.source: The length of each circuit in terms of excitation groups
examples.translation: Ang haba ng bawat circuit sa mga terminong excitation groups
examples.suggested: Ang haba ng bawat circuit, sinusukat sa bilang ng excitation groups

editor_note: Entry 8 is a faithful, natural prerequisite line ("Paggamit ng [Sampler] primitive, na ginagamit sa workflow na ito"), keeps Sampler/primitive in English as the rest of the page does, and has no drift.

The rewritten heading in entry 109 renders "Post-process" as "Post-processing". The meaning is intact and a learner would not be misled. However, it breaks the parallel with the sibling step headings, which keep the English imperative verbatim ("Optimize" [102], "Execute" [107]). It also no longer matches the four-step list in entry 100 ("**Post-process** ng mga resulta"). A native editor would restore "Post-process" so the four Qiskit-pattern steps read as the same set in the list and in the headings.

examples.source: Post-process {#post-process}
examples.translation: Post-processing {#post-process}
examples.suggested: Post-process {#post-process}
examples.why: The sibling step headings keep the English verb form (Optimize, Execute), and entry 100 names this step "Post-process". Switching to the gerund here makes the step name inconsistent across the page. It does not change the meaning.

editor_note: Five of the six rewritten entries are fine: "Paggamit ng oras ng QPU", "Mga Quantum Circuit", "Nilikha ni", "Sinuri ni", and the copyright-notice sentence all match the English. The one problem is entry 109. It renders the Qiskit-pattern step heading "Post-process" as just "Pagpoproseso" ("processing"), which drops the "post-" meaning of "after execution". Its sibling step headings stay in English ("Optimize", "Execute"), so this one is now inconsistent with them and blurs the order of the steps. It won't seriously mislead a reader because entry 110 right below calls it the final step, but an editor would change it to something like "Post-processing" or "Pagpoproseso pagkatapos".

examples.source: Post-process {#post-process}
examples.translation: Pagpoproseso {#post-process}
examples.suggested: Post-process {#post-process} (or: Pagpoproseso pagkatapos {#post-process})
examples.why: This heading is the step that comes after execution. "Pagpoproseso" on its own just means "processing", so it loses the "post-" meaning, and it is the only step heading translated while "Optimize" and "Execute" stay in English.

editor_note: I judged only the two rewritten entries. Entry 128 ("Kung gayon, ang kaukulang quantum state ay:") is faithful and reads naturally. Entry 120 renders the heading "Amplitude encoding" as "Pag-encode ng Amplitude", which literally means encoding the amplitude itself. The technique actually encodes classical data into the amplitudes. The heading also doesn't match the rest of the file: entries 121 and 146 keep "amplitude encoding" in English, and the parallel heading 3.2 in entry 133 keeps "Angle encoding". The definition right after the heading stops a learner from being misled, so this is minor, but the heading should use the same term as the body.

examples.source: 3.1 Amplitude encoding {#31-amplitude-encoding}
examples.translation: 3.1 Pag-encode ng Amplitude {#31-amplitude-encoding}
examples.suggested: 3.1 Amplitude encoding {#31-amplitude-encoding}
examples.why: "Pag-encode ng Amplitude" reads as encoding the amplitude, not encoding data into amplitudes. It also doesn't match the English "amplitude encoding" used in entries 121 and 146, or the parallel heading 3.2 "Angle encoding" (entry 133).
